source: Albrechtsberger, in Mann, The Study of Fugue (1958), p. 261: Ex. 239-240, the perpetual canon for four voices sent to Haydn (1806), 'Solatium miseris socios habuisse dolorum', and Ex. 241, solution 1
transcription: C major: degree 0 = C4 (MIDI 60), so 7 = C5. Durations in beats, quarter = 1, bar = 4 (cut time); 13 bars, the last a rest, then the canon repeats. Bars 1-8 read from Ex. 241's soprano and checked against its alto (a fifth below), tenor (an octave below) and bass (a twelfth below). Bars 9-12 read from Ex. 239's second line (soprano clef), where the scan is unclear, and confirmed against p. 261 of the book (2026-10-18). The entries follow the section signs: one, three and four bars after the dux.
